findings.requirement: specs/proposals/shorter-hashes.md requires ambiguous item IDs to fail explicitly, unsupported/incomplete comparison not to establish equivalence, and required artifacts/dependencies to exist before a success report.
findings.reproduction: Using exact candidate 6a807d8 in three isolated Git fixtures, initialize a catalog and commit items.json containing respectively (1) only item y, (2) two different items both id=x, or (3) item x with duplicate value keys. Register alpha/spec/1 with item_id=x and structured-item/1, then resolve the returned reference.
findings.actual: All three invalid or unresolvable selected items publish alpha/spec/1@1 successfully, and resolve_version succeeds. The helper independently returns absent, ambiguous, and incomplete respectively, but it is never consulted because latest_entry is None.
findings.expected: A first published ordinary structured-item reference must identify a valid, unique selected item. Refuse malformed/ambiguous/incomplete source and handle proven deletion through explicit lifecycle analysis rather than reporting a normal resolvable item.
findings.cause: Structured extraction validation runs only inside latest_entry/same_bindings deduplication; initial allocation bypasses it completely.
findings.fix: Validate the selected structured item before publishing its first revision or taking a different-binding publication path. Preserve explicit absence/deletion distinctions and add the reproduced malformed/ambiguous publication cases before changing production code.

summary: Independent pinned checks confirm distinct high-precision decimals, equivalent signed/scaled zero forms, self-contained source binding, and an incomplete result for the prior 500-array canonicalization case. Approval is withheld because initial structured publication still accepts absent, ambiguous and duplicate-key items and resolution reports success. No source or coordinator state was changed. Review stopped on this concrete publication-validation defect.
